title: Coriander and Lemon Chermoula
summary: Coriander and parsley chopped with garlic, paprika, cumin and a touch of cayenne, sharpened with lemon and whisked with olive oil.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Chop the herbs and spices
steps.text: Put the coriander, parsley, garlic, paprika, cumin, cayenne and salt in the food processor. Pulse in short bursts, scraping down the bowl, until everything is finely and evenly chopped.

steps.title: Add the lemon
steps.text: Pour in the lemon juice and pulse a few more times, just to bring it together.

steps.title: Whisk in the oil
steps.text: Scrape the mixture into the mixing bowl and whisk in the olive oil by hand. Running olive oil through a fast blade can make it taste bitter, so a whisk keeps the flavour clean.

steps.title: Let it settle
steps.text: Leave the chermoula to stand for 15 min so the dried spices hydrate and the garlic mellows. Taste and add a little more salt if needed.

steps.title: Spoon it over
steps.text: Serve it over grilled or pan-fried fish, roast chicken or charred vegetables, or rub some onto fish before cooking as a quick marinade.

tips: If you have preserved lemon, swap a little of the juice for some finely chopped rind for a deeper, more fragrant note.
Dry the herbs well after washing; water left on the leaves dilutes the sauce.
For a smoky version, use half sweet smoked paprika.
Keep any chermoula used as a raw marinade separate from the sauce you serve at the table.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days; the herbs darken after that. Let it sit at room temperature for 10 min and stir before serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
